items.rationale: The model only knows the text it is given on each call. A system prompt line cannot store anything; with an empty list and nothing saved, last week's text is absent. Picking a, b or d shows the belief that the model or provider remembers chats by itself.

Call 1 input is 800. Call 2 input is 800 + 50 + 400 = 1,250. Call 3 input is 1,250 + 50 + 100 = 1,400. Total 800 + 1,250 + 1,400 = 3,450. An answer of 1,400 counts only the last window, and 1,350 counts each piece once; both ignore that each call re-sends the history.

Facts that must outlast a session belong in a saved record the program reads when needed, one student at a time. A 600-name list in the system prompt is paid for on every call; weights do not change while chatting; the message list lives in the program and ends with the session.

items.rationale: Either reason is complete: the whole history, manual included, is re-sent and billed at every call, and accuracy falls when the relevant text is buried in a long context. An answer that the manual does not fit would be wrong here, since the stem says it fits.

The memory tool is client-side: the model requests a file operation and the application runs it, so the file is an ordinary file on disk. Options a, b and c place the memory inside the model or the provider, the mix-up that memory is stored in the model.
